newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 14.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The weekend's concert by Greek composer Mikis Theodorakis in Skopje was a political event par excellence, attended by President of the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia Kiro Gligorov and a significant number of politicians and businessmen from both countries. The concert is considered to be closely related to Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalas's recent visit to Skopje and paves the way for Prime Minister Costas Simitis's stated intention to visit.

--As the 30th anniversary of the April 21 colonels' dictatorship approaches, the majority of Greeks have forgotten the faces of those who battled the junta. Andreas Papandreou, the late founder of ruling PASOK, receives the most votes.

--Andreas Papandreou's widow, Dimitra Liani, and his sons, George and Andrikos, met over the weekend to discuss two issues dividing the two sides - the question of where to erect a monument to the late founder of PASOK and the complicated issue of his former home, now sold. Agreement was reached only on the monument.
--The 720 Greek men to join the Albanian multinational protection force are ready for the signal to depart for the neighbouring country.

--The Council of State is reported to be concerned about certain powers afforded to the finance ministry's new tax shock troops, SDOE. Reports add that the Council is considering calling for changes to the law governing SDOE, such as their right to bear arms.

--Costas Karamanlis, the conservative opposition New Democracy's new leader, receives his first positive report card, with an ALKO opinion poll giving ND 30.4 percent support and ruling party PASOK 25.6 if elections were to be held on Sunday.
--Some 48,000 contract seasonal employees will be taken on in the public sector before and after the Easter break.
--The new code for civil servants is destined to make radical changes to the public sector, Interior Minister Alekos Papadopoulos says.

--Face-to-face contact with the Greek side makes things easier, FYROM President Kiro Gligorov said after the weekend's concert by Theodorakis in Skopje. Skopje, he added, is open to working with Athens on other initiatives. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
